steps.title: Moon Run needs a winning tune
steps.text: When our robot reaches the flag, the game should play a happy tune. We need to make one!

steps.title: A tune goes up and down
steps.text: A tune is notes going up and down, long and short. Listen to one you know!
steps.dad: Sing along, and draw the tune in the air with your finger: up, up, down.

steps.prompt: At the start of Twinkle Twinkle, do the notes go up or down?
steps.reveal: Up! Twin-kle, twin-kle jumps up high.

steps.intro: Bleep sings three notes. Can you copy them? Then Bleep copies you!

steps.title: The five magic notes
steps.text: These five notes always sound good together. So in our Song Maker there are no wrong notes!
steps.dad: These are the pentatonic notes C, D, E, G and A. Lots of first school songs use them.

steps.title: The Sharing Problem
steps.scenario: {commander} and {copilot} are making one tune together. It has eight boxes. How should you share it?

options.label: One does high notes, one does low notes
One does the first half, one the second
Both tap at the same time!

steps.reveal: Real bands do all of these. Some take turns, some have different jobs, and some just play together. Whatever you chose, let's try it now!
steps.followUp: Is your way fair? What would make it fun for both of you?

steps.intro: Make the winning tune! Tap the boxes, press Play, and change it until you love it. Then save it.
Run all the way to the flag and hear your winning tune!

debrief: Hum your tune! What would you change?
